Not more than a third of them are boarders, and the rest, who have in truth, for the last week, begun to be tired of their holidays, will, when they once get out of school, and begin to choose sides for football, be really glad that the term has again commenced.

arxiv-2102-06401.title: SceneRec: Scene-Based Graph Neural Networks for Recommender Systems ISBN: 978-3-89318-084-4 Conference: 24th International Conference on Extending Database Technology (EDBT); March 23-26, 2021; Nicosia, Cyprus
arxiv-2102-06401.creator: Gang Wang, Ziyi Guo, Xiang Li, Dawei Yin, Shuai Ma
arxiv-2102-06401.description: Abstract . Collaborative filtering has been largely used to advance modern recommender systems to predict user preference. A key component in collaborative filtering is representation learning, which aims to project users and items into a low dimensional space to capture collaborative signals.

arxiv-2112-06037.title: Frames With Several Generators Associated with Weyl-Heisenberg Group and Extended Affine Group
arxiv-2112-06037.creator: Divya Jindal, Lalit Kumar Vashisht
arxiv-2112-06037.description: Abstract . We study the construction of Gabor frames and wavelet frames for Weyl-Heisenberg group and extended affine group by using contraction between the affine group and the Weyl-Heisenberg group due to Subag, Baruch, Birman and Mann. Firstly, we give construction of Gabor frames with several generators from a unitary irreducible representation associated to the Weyl-Heisenberg group.

arxiv-2210-00944.title: Attention Distillation: self-supervised vision transformer students need more guidance
arxiv-2210-00944.creator: Kai Wang, Fei Yang (*corresponding author), Joost van de Weijer
arxiv-2210-00944.description: Abstract Self-supervised learning has been widely applied to train high-quality vision transformers (ViT). Unleashing their excellent performance on memory and compute constraint devices is therefore an important research topic. However, how to distill knowledge from one self-supervised ViT to another has not yet been explored.

arxiv-2301-00020.title: Subharmonic Fidelity Revival in a Driven PXP model
arxiv-2301-00020.creator: HaRu K. Park, SungBin Lee
arxiv-2301-00020.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by HaRu K. Park, SungBin Lee. The PXP model hosts a special set of nonergodic states, referred to as quantum many-body scars. One of the consequences of quantum scarring is the periodic revival of the wave function fidelity. It has been reported that quantum fidelity revival occurs in the PXP model for certain product states, and periodic driving of chemical potential can enhance the magnitude of quantum revival, and can even change the frequencies of revival showing the subharmonic response.

arxiv-2304-03428.title: TinyDet: Accurate Small Object Detection in Lightweight Generic Detectors ⋆
arxiv-2304-03428.creator: Shaoyu Chen, Tianheng Cheng, Jiemin Fang, Qian Zhang, Yuan Li, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang
arxiv-2304-03428.description: Abstract Small object detection requires the detection head to scan a large number of positions on image feature maps, which is extremely hard for computation- and energy-efficient lightweight generic detectors. To accurately detect small objects with limited computation, we propose a two-stage lightweight detection framework with extremely low computation complexity, termed as TinyDet.

arxiv-2311-02973.title: Constraining (anti)nuclei measurements relevant for astrophysics with ALICE
arxiv-2311-02973.creator: \firstname Chiara \lastname Pinto \fnsep \firstname \lastname for the ALICE Collaboration
arxiv-2311-02973.description: Abstract Antinuclei can be produced in space either by collisions of high-energy cosmic rays with the interstellar medium or from the annihilation of dark matter particles stemming into standard model particles. High-energy hadronic collisions at accelerators create a suitable environment for producing light (anti)nuclei.

arxiv-2402-08789.title: Leveraging cough sounds to optimize chest x-ray usage in low-resource settings
arxiv-2402-08789.creator: Alexander Philip, Sanya Chawla, Lola Jover, George P. Kafentzis, Joe Brew, Vishakh Saraf, Shibu Vijayan, Peter M. Small, Carlos Chaccour
arxiv-2402-08789.description: Abstract Chest X-ray is a commonly used tool during triage, diagnosis and management of respiratory diseases. In resource-constricted settings, optimizing this resource can lead to valuable cost savings for the health care system and the patients as well as to and improvement in consult time.

arxiv-2406-16504.title: Production of pentaquarks with hidden charm and double strangeness in Ξ b \Xi_{b} and Ω b \Omega_{b} decays
arxiv-2406-16504.creator: E. Oset, L. Roca, M. Whitehead
arxiv-2406-16504.description: Abstract Recently, several pentaquark states P c ​ s ​ s P_{css} , with global flavor c ¯ ​ c ​ s ​ s ​ n \bar{c}cssn , have been predicted within a theoretical framework based on unitary coupled channels.

arxiv-2406-20088.title: Minimax And Adaptive Transfer Learning for Nonparametric Classification under Distributed Differential Privacy Constraints
arxiv-2406-20088.creator: Arnab Auddy, T. Tony Cai, Abhinav Chakraborty
arxiv-2406-20088.description: Abstract This paper considers minimax and adaptive transfer learning for nonparametric classification under the posterior drift model with distributed differential privacy constraints. Our study is conducted within a heterogeneous framework, encompassing diverse sample sizes, varying privacy parameters, and data heterogeneity across different servers.

arxiv-2505-06468.title: Submillimeter observations of the white dwarf pulsar AR Sco Facilities: SMA(radio), VLA(radio) Astronomical Image Processing System ( Wells 1985 ) , Visfit.jl (Barrett, P. 2025, in preparation)
arxiv-2505-06468.creator: Paul E. Barrett, Mark A. Gurwell
arxiv-2505-06468.description: Abstract AR Scorpii, the so called white dwarf pulsar, contains a rapidly rotating magnetic white dwarf (WD; P spin = 117.0564 s) interacting with a cool, red dwarf (RD) companion in a 3.56 hour orbit. It is a strong radio source with an inverted spectral index between 1–200 GHz that is indicative of synchrotron emission.

arxiv-2509-13303.title: Mixed Triplet-Singlet Order Parameter in Decoupled Superconducting 1H Monolayers of Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides
arxiv-2509-13303.creator: Avior Almoalem, Sajilesh Kunhiparambath, Roni Anna Gofman, Yuval Nitzav, Ilay Mangel, Nitzan Ragoler, Jun Fujii, Ivana Vobornik, Francois Bertran, Amit Kanigel, Jonathan Ruhman, Vidya Madhavan
arxiv-2509-13303.description: Abstract Understanding the emergence of unconventional superconductivity, where the order parameter deviates from simple isotropic s-wave pairing, is a central puzzle in condensed matter physics. Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), though generally regarded as conventional superconductors, display signatures of this unusual behavior and thus provide a particularly intriguing platform to explore how exotic states arise.

arxiv-2601-14789.title: Testing the equivalence to thermal states via extractable work under LOCC
arxiv-2601-14789.creator: Toshihiro Yada, Nobuyuki Yoshioka, Takahiro Sagawa
arxiv-2601-14789.description: Abstract Understanding the thermal behavior of quantum many-body pure states is one of the most fundamental issues in quantum thermodynamics. It is widely known that typical pure states yield vanishing work, just as thermal states do, when one restricts to local operations that cannot access correlations among subsystems.

pmc-10801106.title: The ill-fated triad: Roosevelt, Stalin and Churchill-Post-Yalta strokes and the impact on world leaders
pmc-10801106.creator: Eti Muharremi, Gentian Vyshka
pmc-10801106.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The Yalta Conference of 1945 brought together three of the most influential leaders of the 20th century: Franklin D. Roosevelt, Joseph Stalin and Winston Churchill. Surprisingly, all three leaders would go on to suffer strokes after the conference.

pmc-11346208.title: Medical consultants’ experience of collective leadership in complexity: a qualitative interview study
pmc-11346208.creator: Áine Carroll, Jane McKenzie, Claire Collins
pmc-11346208.description: PurposeThe aim of this study was to explore and understand the leadership experiences of medical consultants prior to a major hospital move. Health and care is becoming increasingly complex and there is no greater challenge than the move to a new hospital. Effective leadership has been identified as being essential for successful transition.

pmc-11433443.title: Experimental and Numerical Study of Steel–Concrete Composite Beams Strengthened under Load
pmc-11433443.creator: Piotr Szewczyk
pmc-11433443.description: This study analysed the strengthening process of a classical steel–concrete composite beam. The beam consisted of a reinforced concrete slab connected by shear studs to an IPE steel profile. The key idea was that the composite beam was strengthened under load. This process simulated an actual reinforced structure that is always subjected to dead loads, with possible service loads.

pmc-11518520.title: Integrity and accountability in academic publishing: trends and implications of paper retractions and journal delistings
pmc-11518520.creator: A Valz Gris, A Cristiano, A M Pezzullo
pmc-11518520.description: In the context of academic publishing, ‘retraction’ refers to the withdrawal of a published article from the scientific record due to issues such as significant errors, plagiarism, fraudulent data, or unethical research practices. Retractions play a critical role in maintaining the integrity of scientific literature.

pmc-11639865.title: Endorsement of reporting guidelines and clinical trial registration across urological medical journals: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11639865.creator: Alex Hagood, Joseph Case, Trevor Magee, Caleb Smith, Danya Nees, Griffin Hughes, Matt Vassar
pmc-11639865.description: IntroductionOver the years, funding for urologic diseases has witnessed a steady rise, reaching $587 million in 2020 from $541 million in 2018. In parallel, there has been a notable increase in the total number of urology journals from 2011 to 2018.

pmc-11644339.title: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Poplar: A Novel Transcriptomic-Metabolomic Approach to Evaluating the Impact of Divergent Pruning Strategies
pmc-11644339.creator: Xiaoting Liu, Kewei Cai, Qinhui Zhang, Weizi An, Guanzheng Qu, Luping Jiang, Fusen Wang, Xiyang Zhao
pmc-11644339.description: Pruning is a common forest-tending method; its purpose is to promote growth and improve the overall stand quality. Poplar is a fast-growing, broad-leaved tree species with high ecological and economic value. It is a common management method to promote its growth by pruning and adjusting the spatial structure of the stand, but its potential regulatory mechanism remains unclear.

pmc-11653928.title: Long-term prevalence of PTSD symptom in family members of severe COVID-19 patients: a serial follow-up study extending to 18 months after ICU discharge
pmc-11653928.creator: Nobuyuki Nosaka, Ayako Noguchi, Takashi Takeuchi, Kenji Wakabayashi
pmc-11653928.description: BackgroundExperiencing a loved one's stay in the intensive care unit (ICU) can profoundly affect families, often leading to post-intensive care syndrome-family (PICS-F), a condition particularly exacerbated during the COVID-19 pandemic. While PICS-F significantly impacts the mental health of families of ICU patients, especially in the context of COVID-19, the long-term effects beyond 12 months remain understudied.

pmc-12494014.title: Magnetostratigraphic constraints on the late Ediacaran paleomagnetic enigma
pmc-12494014.creator: James S. Pierce, David A. D. Evans, Dana E. Polomski, Nasrrddine Youbi, Mohamed A. Mediany, Jihane Ounar, Rachid Oukhro, M. Ahmed Boumehdi, Justin V. Strauss, C. Brenhin Keller, Andres Gärtner, Maria Ovtcharova, Jörn-Frederik Wotzlaw, Ulf Linnemann
pmc-12494014.description: Paleogeography of the Ediacaran Period has remained poorly understood because of paleomagnetic studies commonly yielding perplexing or conflicting data. Here, we report new magnetostratigraphic data from the Ediacaran Ouarzazate Group in the Anti-Atlas Mountains of Morocco, which have primary magnetizations supported by a positive conglomerate test and stratigraphically consistent directions within volcanic units across multiple localities.

pmc-13334618.title: Defect‐Functionalization‐Mediated Tunneling Drives Nonlinear Photoemission in Perovskites
pmc-13334618.creator: Hang Ren, Xi Zhang, Yicheng Wang, Shuai Wang, Zhi Wang, Yumeng Li, Jikai Yang, Xin Wang, Weijun Chen, Yining Mu
pmc-13334618.description: The deliberate functionalization of defects represents a largely unexplored frontier in advanced optoelectronics. Within Einstein's photoelectric framework, we elucidate how deep‐level defects in CsPbBr3 films act as functional mediators to govern carrier transport, interfacial electron escape, and quantum efficiency multiplication via a defect‐mediated tunneling process.

pmc-13386800.title: Antibacterial and wound healing activities of AgNPs, ZnONPs, and Fe3O4NPs against Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli
pmc-13386800.creator: Mohammad Hossein Soleimani, Pegah Shakib, Mohammad Reza Zolfaghari, Ashkan Dirbaziyan, Reza Heidari, Mohsen Chamanara, Saeed Khoshnood, Faeze Fallahi
pmc-13386800.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the individual and combined effects of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs), and iron oxide nanoparticles (Fe₃O₄-NPs) on wound healing in a rat model of infection with Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, and to compare their efficacy with a standard antibiotic treatment.
